start.speaker: Kronos
start.text: Alright, my friend, listen up. Aseb is an ancient Egyptian game, and if you want to impress Anubis and claim my Pin with Logo, you need to understand how it works.

ATD2.speaker: Kronos
ATD2.text: The board is divided into squares, and you have five pieces to move. The goal? Get all five of your pieces to the end of the board and off it. Simple as that.

ATD3.speaker: Kronos
ATD3.text: Each turn, you throw the sticks, they work like dice. The number you get represents many squares your piece advances. You can choose which piece to move, but only one piece per turn.

ATD3.extra.speaker: Kronos
ATD3.extra.text: Just, dont be greedy, one piece at a time is fine.

ATD4.speaker: Kronos
ATD4.text: Now here's where it gets interesting: some squares are marked with this symbol. Land on one of those, and you get another throw! Quite the advantage, wouldn't you say?

ATD5.speaker: Kronos
ATD5.text: But watch out—if your piece lands on a square your opponent's piece occupies, their piece gets sent back to the start. Fair's fair, after all.

ATD6.speaker: Kronos
ATD6.text: There's one catch: to get your piece off the board at the very end, you need the *exact* number. No more, no less. If you overshoot, your piece stays put, and you pick another piece to move or end your turn.

ATD7.speaker: Kronos
ATD7.text: If your throw doesn't let you move any piece—maybe all your pieces are stuck or the number is too high—then you lose that turn. The game continues with your opponent.

ATD8.speaker: Kronos
ATD8.text: First one to get all three pieces off the board wins. Once that happens, the match is over, and the victor claims their prize. In your case... well, you'd better win.

ATD9.speaker: Kronos
ATD9.text: The path starts from your side, curves around to the center, and continues toward the end square. Pay attention to where you're moving—one mistake and Anubis will capitalize on it.

ATD10.speaker: Kronos
ATD10.text: Think strategically. Should you move your piece that's closest to the end, or should you develop a piece that's still near the start? Every decision matters when you're playing for keeps.

ATD11.speaker: Kronos
ATD11.text: One more thing—each piece must complete the full path on its own. You can't skip around or take shortcuts. The rules are ancient and absolute.

ATD12.speaker: Kronos
ATD12.text: There you have it. Aseb in a nutshell. Now, are you ready to face the guardian of the underworld? Because I believe in you... mostly.

ATD13.speaker: Kronos
ATD13.text: Oh yeah i almost forgot, if you need to refresh the rules, open the menu and go to help.

ATD14.speaker: Kronos
ATD14.text: An aseb option will be on there for you to check anytime you want.

ATD15.speaker: Kronos
ATD15.text: Good luck, my friend. Now get out there!
